109-1-LB100_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB100_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Economic Development LB100 requires the Director of Economic Development to electronically file an annual report with the Legislature beginning July 1, 2026, showing the percentage and total dollar amount of economic development funds awarded to (1) individuals starting new businesses and (2) individuals/entities providing services to businesses established within the previous five years whose principal place of business is in Nebraska. The bill encourages (but does not mandate) the Department of Economic Development to award five percent of its economic development funds to those categories. Department of Economic Development provisions (effective reporting beginning July 1, 2026):\n\n- The Director must annually file an electronic report with the Legislature (first due July 1, 2026) showing (a) the percentage and (b) the total dollar amount of economic development funds awarded to: (i) individuals starting new businesses or (ii) individuals/entities providing services to businesses established within the past five years whose principal place of business is in Nebraska. \n- Beginning July 1, 2026, the Department is encouraged (not required) to allocate 5% of its economic development funds to those same startups/service providers. \n- "Economic development funds" is defined to include amounts budgeted for DED programs, including community development block grants.\n\nNo mandatory appropriations or binding budget transfers for DED are created; the 5% targeting is advisory. 109-1-LB101_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB101_Intro_Copy.docx LB101 amends the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to: (1) create an explicit right to a jury trial in possession actions — complaints may demand a jury and summonses must notify defendants of that right; (2) specify court and clerk procedures — complaints for restitution filed with the district or county court clerk, summons served within three days and returnable in five, and alternative service under section 76-1442.01 allowed (but bars money judgments when used); (3) impose duties on courts — inform defendants of jury rights at first appearance, schedule bench trials within 10–14 days, schedule jury trials as practicable, and permit courts to require tenants to deposit accrued rent if a tenant-requested jury continuance is granted; and (4) direct issuance of writs of restitution to constables or sheriffs (possession restored within ten days). The bill also bars rental-agreement waivers of state or federal rights and provides tenant remedies; no funding or appropriation changes. Adds notice and procedural protections regarding the right to a jury trial in possession actions. Requirements: complaints must inform defendants of their jury-trial right; at first appearance the court must notify the defendant and, in county court, ask whether the defendant demands a jury or elects a bench trial. Timing rules: bench trials must be set 10–14 days after summons; jury trials are scheduled as soon as practicable. If a tenant requests a continuance of the jury trial beyond the initial date, the court may require the tenant to deposit accrued rent with the clerk of the court. Agencies mentioned: courts (including county courts) and the clerk of the court. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB111_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB111_Intro_Copy.docx LB111 regulates insurer practices for motor vehicle repairs. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no funding, appropriations, or budget changes.\n\nSummary of additions: The bill defines key terms (consumer, consumer care, insurer, nonoriginal equipment manufacturer, part) and imposes consumer protections governing use of aftermarket/non‑OEM parts. Insurers must obtain written consumer consent before using non‑OEM parts, may not charge consumers a price difference if they choose OEM parts, and must provide a 10‑point font notice on estimates. 109-1-LB123_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB123_Final_Copy.docx LB123 amends procedures for the Auditor of Public Accounts and the State Treasurer regarding noncompliant political subdivisions and municipalities.\n\n- Auditor of Public Accounts: prepares budget documents, requires governmental units to submit calculated restricted funds authority, and notifies the governing body and State Treasurer of noncompliance (budget limits or failure to file audits).\n- State Treasurer: upon Auditor notice, suspends distribution of state aid and holds funds for six months; if compliance occurs funds are released, if not the funds are forfeited and redistributed to other county recipients or returned to the Highway Allocation Fund (or to the General Fund for homestead-exemption reimbursements).\n- Municipal audits: failure to file triggers withholding of distributions under sections 39-2511–39-2520; withheld amounts are redistributed after six months if audit remains unfiled.\n- Extended noncompliance (12 months) renders the political subdivision or city/village ineligible for future state distributions until compliance is achieved.\n- Repeals original sections 13-522, 19-2907, and 13-3407. - Auditor of Public Accounts must notify the State Treasurer when a governmental unit is noncompliant; the unit forfeits state aid until the Auditor notifies the Treasurer that it is compliant. \n- Forfeited state aid remains forfeited and is redistributed; if there is no eligible recipient it is returned to the Highway Allocation Fund per subdivision (a)(i). \n- Any political subdivision that fails to reach compliance within 12 months of the Auditor’s delinquency notice is ineligible for future state aid distributions until it becomes compliant. \n- Cities and villages similarly lose entitlement to distributions under sections 39-2511 to 39-2520 until compliance is achieved. 109-1-LB126_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB126_Final_Copy.docx LB126 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §10-126 governing municipal bond redemption. It clarifies which issuers are subject to the five-year optional-call restriction and expressly excludes bonds of public power districts, public power and irrigation districts, metropolitan utilities districts, cities of the metropolitan and primary classes, housing authorities, large revenue or large-issue school district bonds, bonds sold by counties via competitive sale, and bonds issued by the Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska and the Board of Trustees of the Nebraska State Colleges. 109-1-LB127_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB127_Intro_Copy.docx This bill defines “prosecutor” to include the Attorney General (and deputies/assistants), county attorneys (and deputies), city attorneys, or any person with authority to prosecute, and makes those prosecutions subject to statutory damages when charges are dismissed, defendants are acquitted, discharged under timing rules, or convictions overturned. Trial courts must hold hearings to award reasonable attorney fees, litigation expenses (including appeals and postconviction actions), and actual damages (e.g., lost wages). Prosecutors may negotiate dismissals in which a defendant waives damages. The bill amends and repeals provisions of section 29-1208 to incorporate the damages remedy. Added language expressly identifies prosecutors to include the Attorney General, deputy and assistant attorneys general, county attorneys and their deputies, city attorneys, and any other persons with authority to prosecute. It also inserts two items at the end: an unclear fragment "(1) His" and "(2) Damages as provided in section 1 of this act," thereby tying recoverable damages to section 1 of the bill. 109-1-LB128_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB128_Intro_Copy.docx LB128 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §75-426 concerning railroad-accident reporting and the Public Service Commission's (PSC) investigatory authority. The PSC retains the authority to investigate railroad accidents within Nebraska that result in loss of life or injury. The bill requires the railroad corporation operating where an accident occurred to report the incident to the PSC in writing or by telephone within 24 hours and to furnish the PSC a copy of the report it files with the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA). Those reports are inadmissible as evidence in court. Failure to comply is a Class IV misdemeanor. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds authority for "the commission" to investigate causes of all railroad accidents within the state that result in loss of life, personal injury, or property damage. 109-1-LB129_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB129_Intro_Copy.docx LB129 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §13-407 to define "energy source" (including electricity for EV charging, natural gas, propane, diesel, biofuels, hydrogen, etc.) and prohibits counties, cities, villages, and other political subdivisions from adopting ordinances, codes, resolutions, rules, regulations, or policies that restrict or prohibit any such energy source as delivered, used, converted, or supplied by: natural gas utilities; natural gas transmission companies; retail marketers or dispensers of propane; or retail marketers of other energy sources, in serving customers they are authorized to serve. 109-1-LB12_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB12_Intro_Copy.docx LB12 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §25-228 to remove time limitations on civil actions arising from violations of the child sexual assault statutes (sections 28-319.01 and 28-320.01). Civil suits against the individual perpetrator are unlimited if the offense occurred on or after August 24, 2017 (or earlier if not previously time-barred). Civil suits against any other person or entity (not the direct perpetrator) are unlimited for offenses occurring on or after the bill’s effective date (or earlier if not previously time-barred). The State Tort Claims Act and the Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act remain exceptions. Criminal prosecution is not required to pursue a civil action. No agencies, departments, or funding/appropriations are named or modified. The original section is repealed. Adds a provision removing any statute-of-limitations for suits against entities covered by the State Tort Claims Act or the Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act, except where those Acts themselves provide otherwise. The no-time-limit rule applies to violations occurring on or after the bill’s effective date and to earlier violations that were not already time-barred. No agencies, departments, or funding/appropriation changes are referenced. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB130_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB130_Intro_Copy.docx LB130 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-4602 governing General Fund net receipts and transfers to the Cash Reserve Fund. It requires the Tax Commissioner to publish monthly and annual statements comparing actual General Fund net receipts to forecasted and prior-year receipts (forecasts by the Nebraska Economic Forecasting Advisory Board). Within 15 days after each fiscal year the Tax Commissioner must calculate (a) actual minus certified estimated net receipts and (b) 50% of actual receipts times the difference between the most recent annual growth rate and the 20-year average growth (excluding the lowest year). If (a) is positive, the Commissioner certifies the larger amount to the Director of Administrative Services; upon that director’s certification the State Treasurer transfers that amount from the General Fund to the Cash Reserve Fund (immediate transfer of (a) amount, remainder by end of the subsequent fiscal year). Transfers are limited so the Cash Reserve Fund does not exceed 16% of budgeted General Fund expenditures, unless the Legislature authorizes a higher balance. The bill repeals the prior version of the section and takes effect immediately (emergency). Requires the Tax Commissioner, within 15 days after each fiscal year, to calculate: (i) actual General Fund net receipts minus the certified estimate, and (ii) 50% of actual receipts times the amount the most recent annual growth exceeds the 20‑year average growth (excluding the lowest year). If (i) is positive, the Commissioner must certify the larger of the two amounts to the Director of Administrative Services. Upon that certification, the State Treasurer transfers that amount from the General Fund to the Cash Reserve Fund: an amount equal to (i) immediately, with any remainder by the end of the next fiscal year. Transfers are reduced so the Cash Reserve Fund does not exceed 16% of budgeted General Fund expenditures (excluding reappropriations/encumbrances), though the Legislature may authorize a higher balance for capital or emergency needs. 109-1-LB135_Intro E and R Engrossing Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB135_Intro_Copy.docx LB135 standardizes election procedures for school-related fiscal measures and clarifies agency responsibilities.\n\nKey agency changes\n- Election commissioner/county clerk: designated to conduct school bond, levy, budget-exceedance, and related elections in compliance with subsection (3) of §32-559; may bill school districts directly for special-election costs (§32-1203).\n- School boards/school districts and educational service units: required elector approval under §32-559 for bonds, levy increases, exceeding allowable growth, lease‑purchase approvals, teacherage taxes, and certain budget authority increases.\n- Joint entities/joint public agencies: may not issue bonds tied to allocated property tax levy authority until each participating school district’s electors approve under §32-559; levy allocations to joint public agencies must be reported to the Property Tax Administrator (§13-2507, §13-809).\n- Secretary of State and Auditor of Public Accounts: retained roles in election cancellation/recording when meeting procedures are used to approve growth exceptions (§13-519, §13-809).\n\nBudget/fiscal effects\n- Reaffirms voter approval requirements to exceed budgeted restricted funds, allowable growth, and levy limits; aligns timing/notice and canvass procedures with county election officials.\n- Election cost allocation: political subdivisions pay election costs; school districts can be billed directly for special elections. Adds procedures tying school-district elections to compliance with subsection (3) of §32-559 and assigns specific duties to local election officials. Key agencies/departments named:\n- School board: files/certifies ballot questions by deadlines (Mar 1 for primaries, Sept 1 for general, eighth Friday before local general), certifies lists of out‑of‑county registered voters five days before the election, and receives returns for canvass.\n- Election commissioner or county clerk: conducts/counts the election; furnishes early‑voting ballots not less than 21 days prior; publishes/sample‑ballot and mail‑notice duties; may appoint two disinterested persons to assist in counting; coordinates cross‑county registration certs and ballot distribution.\n- Receiving board: delivers ballots to the election commissioner/county clerk after polls close.\n\nBudget/funding change: two disinterested persons on the counting board must be paid no less than the minimum hourly rate in §48‑1203. No other appropriations or new funding lines are added. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB140_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB140_Final_Copy.docx LB140 requires each school board of a Nebraska public school district to develop and adopt a policy governing student use of electronic communication devices. The bill prohibits schools from monitoring, collecting, or accessing information on devices not owned by or provided for academic use by the district. The act takes effect immediately upon passage due to an emergency clause. Adds two justifications for school-run monitoring: (iv) to monitor or manage a student's health care, and (v) when the school board or an appropriate school employee determines it appropriate. Also clarifies the section does not authorize monitoring, collecting, or accessing data on electronic devices that are not owned by, or provided for academic use by, the school district. 109-1-LB155_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB155_Intro_Copy.docx LB155 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 28-1406, 28-1409, and 28-1410. It also clarifies that an actor lawfully present in a motor vehicle need not retreat from that vehicle unless the actor was the initial aggressor, and that neither the actor nor the person being protected must retreat farther when lawfully present in another's motor vehicle than from their own. Violations of the section are punishable as a Class II misdemeanor. The bill repeals the original sections. The Judiciary Committee handled the bill; no executive agency is specifically named in the text provided, and the bill includes no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes. Adds a clause clarifying that a program participant is covered when retrieving or disposing of syringes, needles, or other related items at or within the immediate vicinity of the program site or facility. 109-1-LB168_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB168_Final_Copy.docx LB168 enacts the "340B Contract Pharmacy Protection Act." It prohibits manufacturers (and their agents, affiliates, or third-party logistics providers) from denying, restricting, or prohibiting acquisition or delivery of 340B drugs to locations authorized by 340B entities, and from conditioning such access on submission of non‑federally required data. Enforcement authority is granted to the Nebraska Attorney General and any county attorney to seek injunctions or other relief in the name of the State of Nebraska. The bill cites federal 42 U.S.C. 256b, includes severability, and takes effect immediately by emergency clause. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds the "340B Contract Pharmacy Protection Act," defining "340B drug," "340B entity," and "Manufacturer" by reference to federal statutes. Prohibits manufacturers, their agents/affiliates, and third‑party logistics providers from denying or restricting acquisition or delivery of 340B drugs to locations authorized by 340B entities, or from conditioning access on submission of provider/claim/purchasing/medical/utilization data, except where federal law requires otherwise. Enforcement: the Nebraska Attorney General or any county attorney may sue in the name of the State for injunctions or other relief to stop violations. Includes a savings clause that the Act must be applied consistently with federal law. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB169_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB169_Intro_Copy.docx LB169 directs the Nebraska Department of Revenue to expand its Tax Expenditure Report to include estimated revenue losses from failure to impose sales and use tax on services purchased for nonbusiness use and to list many specific service categories. The bill broadens the definition of "gross receipts" to bring numerous services (e.g., vehicle and property maintenance, animal specialty and veterinary services except livestock, personal care, landscaping, many professional and entertainment services, telefloral delivery, travel agency services, etc.) within the sales/use tax base and repeals several statutory sales-tax exemptions. It clarifies that the Mechanical Amusement Device occupation tax is in addition to state taxes, including sales and use tax, and prohibits political subdivisions from levying other taxes on such devices except local option sales and use taxes. Operative date: October 1, 2025. No direct appropriations or new budget allocations are included. Summary: The added text expands a list of gross‑income exemptions to cover numerous services (chartered flights; clothing cleaning; dating; hair care except cutting; interior design; lobbying; chartered local passenger transport; marketing/telemarketing; massage; nail care; personal instruction; sightseeing by ground vehicle; skin care; swimming pool cleaning/maintenance; tattoo/body modification; telefloral delivery; travel agency services; and weight‑loss services). It also addresses sales and use tax for gross receipts from operation of mechanical amusement devices, excluding local option sales and use taxes. No specific state or federal agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB16_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB16_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Military Department The bill amends state motor‑vehicle lettering law to add/clarify exemptions for vehicles of the Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, and the Military Department. 109-1-LB170_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB170_Intro_Copy.docx LB170 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-2704.24 to remove the sales-tax exemptions for candy and soft drinks, redefines related terms (candy, soft drinks, prepared food, etc.), and takes effect October 1, 2025. The bill text cross-references the federal Food and Drug Administration for recommended cooking guidance and was referred to the Legislature’s Revenue Committee. No state agency (beyond these references) is explicitly assigned new duties in the text, and the bill contains no changes to appropriations, funding, or budget allocations. Adds definitions for "candy" and "soft drinks." "Candy" is defined as sugar/honey or sweetener preparations combined with chocolate, fruits, nuts, etc., in bar/drop/piece form and excludes preparations containing flour or requiring refrigeration. "Soft drinks" are defined as nonalcoholic beverages with natural or artificial sweeteners and exclude beverages containing milk or milk substitutes or beverages with more than 50% vegetable or fruit juice. 109-1-LB171_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB171_Intro_Copy.docx LB171 amends Nebraska income tax law. It (1) modifies individual income tax rate schedules, phasing certain top bracket rates downward so that "rate three" becomes 4.99% and "rate four" becomes 4.99% effective for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026; (2) changes corporate rates to a flat 5.20% for 2025 and a flat 4.99% for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026. The bill retains Tax Commissioner duties to adjust brackets for inflation, publish updated rate schedules and tax tables, and sets indexing based on the Consumer Price Index (Bureau of Labor Statistics) and prior Internal Revenue Code provisions. 109-1-LB172_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB172_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services LB172 requires the Department of Correctional Services to order mental-health evaluations for certain incarcerated persons (specified sex-offense convictions or repeat registrants) to determine whether they are dangerous sex offenders. Evaluations must be ordered at least 180 days before scheduled release, with written findings provided no later than 150 days before release, and prosecuting authorities must be notified. Persons who refuse or fail to complete sex-offender treatment offered by DCS or the Department of Health and Human Services are included, though inability to complete due to insufficient time or programming is not treated as refusal. The Department of Health and Human Services is designated recipient for sexual‑assault reports involving victims under 18; confidential victim information may be shared with DHHS for child abuse/neglect investigations, and DHHS may request the Attorney General’s Child Protection Division to investigate or prosecute if a county attorney declines. No appropriations or budgetary changes for DCS or DHHS are specified. Summary of added text (focus requested agencies):\n\n- The additions primarily expand and clarify definitions (e.g., "covered offense," "electronic communication device," "indistinguishable," and related child‑pornography terms), specify affirmative defenses, and set age‑based penalties: under 19 = Class III felony; 19 or older = Class ID felony; prior covered‑offense conviction = Class IC felony. \n- There are no provisions that mention, modify, or assign duties to the Department of Correctional Services or the Department of Health and Human Services. \n- No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. 109-1-LB174_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB174_Intro_Copy.docx LB174 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §25-1558 to add a distinct, lower garnishment limit for medical debt sought by medical debt buyers or medical creditors. For such debts garnishment may not exceed the lesser of: 10% of disposable earnings for the week; the amount by which disposable earnings exceed 30 times the federal minimum hourly wage; or, where the creditor alleges specific facts in a sworn affidavit, 20% if the individual is not a head of family. The bill defines “medical debt,” “medical debt buyer,” “medical creditor,” and “health care services.” The Commissioner of Labor is authorized to promulgate a regulation converting the wage threshold for nonweekly pay periods. The original section is repealed. No funding or appropriations are specified. Added provisions cap wage garnishment for medical debt to the lesser of: (a) 10% of disposable weekly earnings; (b) the amount by which weekly disposable earnings exceed 30 times the federal minimum hourly wage (29 U.S.C. 206(a)(1)); or (c) 20% if the debtor is shown by the creditor’s sworn affidavit not to be a head of household. The text also defines “health care services,” “medical debt,” “medical debt buyer,” and “medical creditor.” No government agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes. 109-1-LB175_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB175_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Transportation Amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §74‑1335 to allow an interested landowner whose property lies on both sides of a railroad right‑of‑way to file a written complaint with the Nebraska Department of Transportation alleging an inadequate or unsafe crossing. 109-1-LB176_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB176_Intro_Copy.docx LB176 amends §86‑1304 of the Nebraska Broadband Bridge Act. It clarifies application requirements administered by the commission: applicants (providers, cooperatives, political subdivisions, Indian tribes) must meet matching‑fund rules (50% outside high‑cost areas, 25% inside; federal funds excluded), provide service scalable to 100/100 Mbps, and meet commission‑published application deadlines. Applications from political subdivisions or tribes must be public‑private partnerships with a provider. Applicants must complete projects within 18 months (extensions allowed) or repay grants on a specified monthly schedule; failure to meet speed tests after remediation also triggers repayment. New required local approvals: a resolution from each county/city/village in the project area including a map, permit acknowledgement, and timeline. Applicants are barred from using equipment on the FCC Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau's Covered List. No changes to state appropriations or budget allocations are included. Adds a requirement that applicants must include, with their application, a resolution of project support adopted by each county, city, and village where the project will be located. Each resolution must at minimum contain a map of the project area, an acknowledgement that the applicant will seek appropriate permits, and a proposed project timeline. No state agencies, departments, or funding/appropriation changes are mentioned. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB178_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB178_Intro_Copy.docx This bill directs the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission to establish and administer a mandatory server alcohol-training program (effective Jan. 1, 2026), approve provider programs, require issuance of completion certificates and submission of participant names, and enforce employer compliance (licenses may be suspended, canceled, or revoked). The commission may set enrollment fees (not to exceed $30) and certification fees (not to exceed $20) to defray administrative costs, including salary and benefits. All fees collected are remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission Rule and Regulation Cash Fund. The fund’s uses are expanded to include administering the new training requirement; funds may be transferred to the General Fund by the Legislature and are invested by the state investment officer under existing state investment law. Creates a mandatory server alcohol-training program to be run by the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission (the commission) under section 6 and 53-117.03. The commission may charge an enrollment fee up to $30; all fees are collected by the commission and remitted to the State Treasurer for deposit to the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission Rule and Regulation Cash Fund. Effective January 1, 2026, retail licensees may only employ staff who have completed commission‑approved training and obtained certification (or obtain certification within 90 days). Licensees must keep employee certificates (or proof of <90 days employment) on the premises. The commission may suspend, cancel, or revoke licenses for noncompliance. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB179_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB179_Final_Copy.docx LB179 amends Nebraska retirement statutes affecting cities of the first class and their public safety retirement systems. Key agency/financial provisions:\n\n- Police: Section 16-1005 raises the employee contribution rate for police officers from 7% to 9% of salary effective October 1, 2025. Cities of the first class continue to "pick up" these contributions (treated as employer contributions for federal tax purposes under IRC §414(h)) and must pay them from the same municipal payroll funding sources; employees may not opt out. Voluntary contributions and interest-crediting rules remain.\n\n- Firefighters: Section 16-1027 directs the retirement committee and funding medium to offer optional benefit forms permitting single lump-sum or one-or-more partial payments of a firefighter’s retirement value (applicable to retirees on/after Jan 1, 1997). If a minimum statutory pension cannot be provided from a firefighter’s retirement value, the city must use funds from the retirement system’s unallocated employer account to satisfy the benefit.\n\n- Operative date: Benefit-form changes (Sections 2 and 4) become effective October 1, 2025. Adds two provisions: (1) Beginning October 1, 2025, each police officer must contribute 9% of salary to the (public) retirement system. (2) Grants firefighters, upon retirement, the option to receive their retirement value as a single lump sum or as one or more partial payments in amounts and at frequencies they elect. No specific state agency is named beyond the retirement system, and no explicit appropriations, budget allocations, or funding transfers are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB17_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB17_Intro_Copy.docx LB17 amends the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to restrict most landlord fees, allow limited specified fees (rent, security deposit per §76-1416, NSF fee limited to landlord cost, late fee cap, application fee limited to actual cost of obtaining a consumer report), and impose detailed application-fee and consumer-reporting procedures. Landlords must provide prospective tenants copies of any consumer reports obtained and written notices identifying each consumer reporting agency (name/address/phone) and advising tenants of their rights to access and dispute consumer-report information. The bill ties enforcement to Nebraska’s Consumer Protection Act: violations may be pursued by the aggrieved person or the Attorney General and may carry civil penalties up to $300 per violation plus court costs and attorney fees. It references compliance with the state Credit Report Protection Act and the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Added provisions regulate landlord fees and tenant screening. Agencies/departments mentioned or implicated:\n- Consumer reporting agencies / credit reporting agencies: landlords may charge an application fee up to the actual cost of obtaining a consumer report, must provide applicants a copy of any consumer/tenant screening report, and must disclose the name, address, and phone number of each agency and applicants’ dispute/access rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (including sections 616–617, 15 U.S.C. 1681n & 1681o).\n- Attorney General: enforcement role — violations are Consumer Protection Act violations (section 59‑1602) enforceable by the aggrieved person or the Attorney General; violating landlords may face up to $300 per violation plus costs and attorney fees.\n- References to state criminal-history statutes (sections 29‑3527 and 43‑2,108.05) and section 76‑1416 (security deposit rules).\n\nNo changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. 109-1-LB181_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB181_Intro_Copy.docx LB181 requires the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to expand the Young Adult Bridge to Independence program to cover young adults not lawfully present in the United States. DHHS must: (1) submit state-plan amendments to seek federal Title IV‑E funding for newly eligible young adults (deadline listed) and implement the program consistent with federal Fostering Connections requirements; and (2) by October 1, 2025, apply to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to amend the Medicaid state plan to provide Title XIX/XXI medical assistance (including CHIP) to participating young adults, including those under 21 not lawfully present. If youth are ineligible for Title XIX/XXI, DHHS must pursue other coverage options, including payment from the state General Fund. DSS rulemaking deadlines and repeal of prior sections are included. If they are not eligible for those federal programs, "the department" must pursue other coverage options, including payment from the state's General Fund. By October 1, 2025, the department must apply to the federal Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to amend the Medicaid state plan to cover participating young adults (including those under 21 who are not lawfully present). No specific appropriation or dollar amounts are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB182_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB182_Final_Copy.docx Department of Revenue Key provisions referencing the Department of Revenue:\n\n- Defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue for the Child Care Tax Credit Act. \n- Affordable Housing Tax Credit: pass‑through entities or taxpayers allocating, transferring, selling, or assigning credits must notify the Department of Revenue (including transferee tax ID) at least 30 days before a return claiming the credit; notification format prescribed by the Department. \n- Recapture: Nebraska affordable housing tax credits recaptured or disallowed increase the taxpayer's liability in the year the Department of Revenue declares the recapture/disallowance. \n- Child Care Tax Credit: taxpayers apply to the Department (documentation required); the Department approves/certifies credits, considers applications in receipt order, and may approve credits up to an annual cap of $2,500,000. \n- Department may only use DHHS verification information for direct administration of the child care credit. Adds rules requiring pass-through entities and taxpayers to notify the Department of Revenue at least 30 days before claiming or using allocated, transferred, sold, or assigned Nebraska affordable housing tax credits, providing the transferee's tax identification number in a department-prescribed format. Credits may be allocated among partners/members/shareholders, further reallocated, or sold/assigned; they may offset individual income taxes, certain insurer premium/retaliatory taxes, and franchise taxes. A taxpayer using the credit against retaliatory taxes is not subject to additional retaliatory tax, and any claimed credit is treated as a tax payment for purposes of section 77-2734.03. The changes apply to taxable years beginning or deemed to begin on or after Jan. 1, 2024. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB183_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB183_Final_Copy.docx LB183 amends the Uniform Disposition of Unclaimed Property Act, primarily affecting the State Treasurer's administration of unclaimed property. 109-1-LB184_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB184_Intro_Copy.docx LB184 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. sections governing tobacco licensing to regulate nitrous oxide. It (1) prohibits tobacco specialty stores from selling or distributing objects containing nitrous oxide and makes violations subject to misdemeanor penalties and possible court-ordered license revocation; (2) bars delivery sales of nitrous-oxide-containing objects by licensed retailers and makes knowingly transporting them via common carrier a Class I misdemeanor; and (3) bans sale/distribution of devices specifically designed for inhaling nitrous oxide for recreational use. All unlawfully sold items are subject to seizure, forfeiture, and destruction, with costs charged to the violator. The cigarette tax division of the Tax Commissioner may revoke or suspend affected licenses after notice and hearing. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds prohibitions and penalties on sale, distribution, and transport of objects containing nitrous oxide, especially by holders of tobacco specialty store licenses (refs. §§28-1420 to 28-1429). Violations carry misdemeanor penalties (ranging from Class III to Class I/II depending on offense and provision), possible license revocation by a court, and designation as a deceptive trade practice under the Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act. Common carriers that knowingly transport such items are criminally liable. All unlawfully sold items are subject to seizure, forfeiture, and destruction, with costs charged to the person from whom they are seized. 109-1-LB205_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB205_Intro_Copy.docx LB205 restricts admissible evidence and damages for past and future medical expenses by using payer-based measures and statutory rate benchmarks. For claimants without private coverage (or on Medicare/Medicaid), recoverable medical damages are capped at 120% of the applicable Medicare reimbursement rate or, where no Medicare rate exists, 170% of the applicable state Medicaid rate. The bill requires disclosure of health coverage, letters of protection, and any sale of medical accounts receivable (including purchaser identity and purchase price). It limits total recoverable medical damages to amounts paid, amounts due, and reasonable necessary future care. The bill also imposes a $1,000,000 cap on noneconomic damages per plaintiff in actions involving commercial motor vehicles requiring a commercial driver's license; courts must first determine full noneconomic damages and then reduce awards to the cap. Medicare and state Medicaid rates are expressly used as benchmarks. No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included. Adds rules governing admissible evidence and caps for medical damages in personal injury/wrongful death cases. It explicitly references Medicare and Medicaid (including state Medicaid rates and federal Social Security Act §1396d(l)(2)(B) as of Jan 1, 2025) as the pricing benchmarks: unpaid past or future medical charges are limited to 120% of applicable Medicare rates (or, if no Medicare rate, 170% of the applicable state Medicaid rate). It requires disclosure when medical receivables are sold to factoring companies. Also imposes a $1,000,000 cap on noneconomic damages in actions involving commercial motor vehicles. 109-1-LB211_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB211_Intro_Copy.docx LB211 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §13-3403 (Property Tax Growth Limitation Act). For fiscal years beginning July 1, 2025, a political subdivision’s preliminary property tax request authority is set at the amount levied by the county board of equalization in the prior year, less exceptions used under §13-3404. It permits additional year-to-year increases based on (a) the subdivision’s growth percentage and (b) an inflation-based percentage. If public safety (per §13-320) comprises ≥20% of a subdivision’s property-tax-funded budget, the inflation component uses the greater of zero or the inflation percentage; if <20%, the inflation floor is the greater of 2% or the inflation percentage. No direct appropriations or new agency budgets are created. The bill takes effect immediately under an emergency clause. Adds a formula altering local governments' (political subdivisions') property tax request authority based on the share of their property-tax-funded budget spent on "public safety services" (as defined in §13-320). The allowable increase equals two components, each computed on prior-year property taxes minus exceptions used under §13-3404(1) and (2): (1) the base growth percentage; and (2) an inflation component. If public safety ≥20% of the property-tax-funded budget, the inflation component is the greater of zero or inflation. If public safety <20%, the inflation component is the greater of 2% or inflation. No direct appropriations or dollar amounts are specified. DOCX | PDF

Seller liability for tax remains when both parties are licensed under §77-4009. Collections are to be used and distributed pursuant to §77-4025. No specific state agency or department is named in the bill, and no new appropriations or budget allocations are specified. The act is operative October 1, 2025, and repeals the original §77-4008. Adds a tax provision imposing a 20% tax on cigars, cheroots, and stogies—calculated either on the purchase price paid by the first owner or on the price at which a first owner who made or manufactured them sells to others—with a maximum tax of $0.50 per cigar. 109-1-LB213_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB213_Intro_Copy.docx LB213 amends section 79-760.01 to require the State Board of Education to adopt measurable K–12 science standards for human embryology by March 1, 2026, and require school districts to integrate them by the 2026–27 school year. 109-1-LB216_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB216_Intro_Copy.docx LB216 restructures district court clerk functions and shifts fiscal responsibility to the judicial branch. Key agencies impacted:\n\n- Nebraska Supreme Court / State Court Administrator: assumes employment of elected district court clerks and their staff beginning January 7, 2027; becomes responsible for salaries, benefits, expenses (funded by appropriations to the Supreme Court), personnel rules, and receipt of transferred books/files. State Court Administrator will negotiate child‑support cost‑reimbursement agreements (effective Jan 1, 2026) and federal reimbursements are credited to Agency 5 – Supreme Court via the State Treasurer.\n\n- Counties / County boards: must provide transfer data, transfer accrued sick leave (up to 1,440 hours) and vacation (up to 280 hours), and reimburse the state (25% of sick‑leave value, 100% of vacation‑leave value transferred). Counties retain ownership of furniture/equipment; retirement cost sharing between county and state is required; metropolitan/primary class counties have alternate retirement provisions.\n\n- Department of Health and Human Services: will receive statistical reporting coordinated by the State Court Administrator.\n\nThe bill eliminates the elected clerk of district court office and creates consolidated clerk offices; effective dates and transitional provisions are specified. Effective Jan. 7, 2027, elected clerks of the district courts and their employees become state employees under the Nebraska Supreme Court. The State of Nebraska, using funds appropriated to the Supreme Court, will pay all salaries, benefits, and expenses of transferred staff; no loss of income is allowed. Counties must provide accrual info for sick/vacation leave. Counties retain furniture/equipment but must transfer books/files to the State Court Administrator. Leave-transfer rules: up to 1,440 sick hours and 280 vacation hours transferable with county reimbursements (sick: county pays 25% of transferred value; vacation: county pays 100% of transferred value); various reimbursements for granted leave and excess balances are specified. Retirement treatment references the Retirement System for Nebraska Counties and the State Employees Retirement System; costs are to be shared proportionately. Transferred employees and dependents may join the Nebraska State Insurance Program without a waiting period. Federal reimbursements for direct child-support costs are to be transferred to the State Treasurer for credit to Agency 5 – Supreme Court. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB222_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB222_Intro_Copy.docx This bill amends duties and enforcement authority for peace officers, the Superintendent of Law Enforcement and Public Safety, and officers of the Nebraska State Patrol (including carrier enforcement officers/ division references) and harmonizes Nebraska Rules of the Road provisions. 109-1-LB224_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB224_Intro_Copy.docx LB224 requires the State of Nebraska (state employers) to provide paid maternity leave to eligible state employees: twelve weeks for full-time employees, prorated for part-time. Leave may be used only after birth and within six months, generally not intermittently unless agreed in writing or certified by a health care provider. The leave runs concurrently with the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (29 U.S.C. 2601 et seq.). The state may not charge this maternity leave to sick, vacation, compensatory, or other leave, must restore the employee to the same or equivalent position after leave, and may not pay out unused maternity leave at separation. No agencies beyond “the state” and FMLA are named; the bill contains no appropriations or funding changes. Creates a state-paid maternity leave program for state employees: full‑time employees get 12 weeks paid leave (part‑time prorated) to bond after birth. Leave may not start before birth, must be used within six months, generally is not intermittent (unless agreed in writing or certified by a health care provider), and runs concurrently with the federal Family and Medical Leave Act. Definitions include "state employee," "maternity leave eligible employee," and "retaliatory action" (prohibited). The leave is not charged against sick, vacation, compensatory, or other leave (except as required by FMLA). No payout on termination; employees must be restored to the same or equivalent position. No specific agencies, departments, or funding/appropriations are named or altered. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB226_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB226_Intro_Copy.docx LB226 allows courts to set aside convictions or juvenile adjudications for defined "concealed weapon" offenses and directs that, once set aside, movants may seek sealing of criminal history records. Courts must notify the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice, the Nebraska State Patrol, and relevant law enforcement agencies, county attorneys, and city attorneys and order those entities to seal records. The bill expands private causes of action under the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act, permitting suits (including damages, equitable relief, or mandamus) against the state, state agencies, political subdivisions, and their officers/employees; it waives sovereign immunity for such suits, removes them from the State and Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Acts, and sets a limitations period (generally four years, with a special January 1, 2029 cutoff). The Attorney General may be asked by the Commission to bring actions. No appropriations or funding changes. Adds a post-conviction process letting people convicted or adjudicated for "concealed weapon offenses" move to set aside convictions after completion of sentence/disposition. Courts must consider post‑conviction behavior and recidivism risk, may grant relief if in the public interest, and there is a rebuttable presumption in favor of relief when the underlying conduct would not now violate current section 28‑1202. If granted, the court must allow sealing of the related criminal history per the cited statutes.\n\nCreates a private right of action against the state, any state agency or political subdivision, and their officers/employees for violations of rules under the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act, waiving sovereign immunity and permitting damages and equitable relief. Such suits are excluded from the State Tort Claims Act and Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act. Provides filing deadlines (four years after accrual or by Jan 1, 2029 for certain older claims). No appropriations or funding changes. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB249_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB249_Intro_Copy.docx LB249 amends the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act. It directs the Nebraska Department of Education to establish "military impact funding" beginning FY2025‑26 for districts that received Section 7003 federal impact aid and educate children of active‑duty service members; the payment equals (per‑pupil local general‑fund tax levy minus per‑pupil federal impact aid) multiplied by the number of such students, floored at zero. The bill revises components of local system formula resources (including adding a percentage of foundation aid for FY2023‑24 and FY2024‑25 and other adjustments). It voids any state aid, budget authority, or reserve certifications for FY2025‑26 completed before the act’s effective date. The Department must certify district budget authority and applicable allowable reserve percentages on or before June 15, 2025 and on or before March 1 annually thereafter. The Legislature’s Appropriations Committee must include amounts necessary to fund those certified state aid amounts in its annual recommendations. Adds a requirement that the (state) department (presumably the Department of Education) determine and pay "military impact funding" to school districts beginning in school fiscal year 2025–26 and thereafter. Eligibility: districts that received a basic support federal impact aid payment under section 7003 of the federal ESEA in the prior year and educate federally connected children of active-duty service members. Formula: per‑pupil federal impact aid = prior year basic support payment ÷ number of active‑duty federally connected students (fall count); per‑pupil general fund tax levy = prior year local property tax levy receipts ÷ fall membership excluding those federally connected students. Military impact funding = (per‑pupil general fund tax levy − per‑pupil federal impact aid) × number of active‑duty students; funding is zero if the difference is negative. No specific new appropriation or funding source is designated. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB24_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB24_Intro_Copy.docx LB24 amends probation fee and revocation statutes. District and county courts must charge a $30 one‑time administrative enrollment fee and monthly programming fees ($25 for standard probation; $35 for intensive supervision and for participants in non‑probation programs using probation personnel). Clerks remit collected fees to the State Treasurer for credit to the Probation Program Cash Fund. Probationers (including those received under section 29‑2637 or the Interstate Compact for Adult Offender Supervision and participants in qualifying interlocal non‑probation programs) are eligible for fee waivers if previously found indigent or, after hearing, if payment would be an undue hardship. Courts may revoke probation for nonpayment except where the probationer is financially unable. Revocation procedures require clear-and-convincing proof; felony probationers face revocation for substance‑abuse/noncriminal violations only after 90 cumulative days of custodial sanctions. Added text lets courts waive fees under §29‑2262(2)(m) and (o) in whole or part for defendants previously found indigent in the case or when payment would cause undue hardship; waivers apply only while the probationer/participant cannot pay monthly probation-programming fees. It also permits extending a probation term, at the joint request of the probationer and the prosecutor, while a revocation motion is pending or until the statutory maximum, so long as the probationer has counsel or makes the request knowingly on the record. Agencies implicated: the courts (judiciary), probation/community corrections, and prosecutors. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB252_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB252_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services, when establishing and maintaining the Medicaid formulary and preferred drug list, to ensure no FDA‑approved non‑opioid pain medication is disadvantaged or discouraged relative to any opioid/narcotic. Prohibited practices include designating a non‑opioid as nonpreferred when an opioid is preferred and applying more restrictive utilization controls (e.g., prior authorization, step therapy) to non‑opioids than the least restrictive opioid controls. The requirement applies immediately upon FDA approval and to drugs provided under department contracts with managed care organizations. No changes to DHHS funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Requires the Department of Health and Human Services, when setting and maintaining the Medicaid formulary and preferred drug list, to ensure FDA‑approved non‑opioid pain drugs are not disadvantaged or discouraged compared with opioids. Prohibited actions include marking a non‑opioid nonpreferred if an opioid is preferred and imposing more restrictive utilization controls (e.g., prior authorization, step therapy) on a non‑opioid than the least‑restrictive control applied to an opioid. Preferences among opioids or among non‑opioids remain allowed. The rule applies immediately upon FDA approval and to drugs provided under DHHS contracts with managed care organizations. 109-1-LB253_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB253_Intro_Copy.docx LB253 requires coverage of biomarker testing by health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and the Nebraska medical assistance program (Medicaid, administered by the Department of Health and Human Services). Coverage must be provided for diagnosis, treatment, management, or monitoring when supported by medical/scientific evidence, including FDA approvals/labels, CMS national or local coverage determinations, Medicare administrative contractor determinations, and nationally recognized guidelines. Insurers must minimize care disruptions (e.g., multiple biopsies). Prior authorization decisions are required within 72 hours for nonurgent and 24 hours for urgent requests for both commercial plans and Medicaid; appeal/exception processes must be posted on insurer websites and DHHS's website. Contracted Medicaid providers must offer testing at the same scope, duration, and frequency as the program. The bill sets a Medicaid implementation date of January 1, 2026. No explicit appropriations or funding changes are specified. Requires the state medical assistance program (and private health insurers, nonprofit plans, HMOs) to cover biomarker testing — by Jan 1, 2026 for the medical assistance program — when supported by medical/scientific evidence, specifically citing: FDA-approved/cleared test indications, FDA‑indicated tests for FDA‑approved drugs, FDA drug label warnings/precautions, CMS national or Medicare administrative contractor local coverage determinations, and nationally recognized clinical guidelines. Entities contracting with the medical assistance program must provide equivalent scope, duration, and frequency. Prior‑authorization decisions must be communicated within 72 hours (nonurgent) or 24 hours (urgent). Insurers and the medical assistance program (or their third‑party agents) must provide clear, accessible exception and adverse‑determination appeal processes on their websites; the medical assistance program must post its process on the Department of Health and Human Services website. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB256_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB256_Intro_Copy.docx LB256 adopts the Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact and creates a regional commission to coordinate interstate passenger-rail planning and advocacy. Commission membership includes each Governor (or designee), a gubernatorial private-sector appointee, and two state legislators per member state. Finance provisions require compacting states to appropriate operating funds by equal apportionment when authorized by their legislatures; the commission may accept federal, state, local, and private donations and grants, but may not issue debt and must submit budgets to each party state's designated officer. Nebraska-specific provisions bar the State of Nebraska from participating in or appropriating any funds (including for planning) for compact rail projects unless the specific project is authorized by a legislative bill. The bill creates the Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact Cash Fund, payable for compact initiatives and investable by the state investment officer under state investment laws. Creates a Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact commission to coordinate Midwestern passenger/high‑speed rail advocacy, planning, project oversight, and intergovernmental cooperation. Agencies/departments referenced: federal agencies, state and local transportation agencies, Governors and state legislatures, legislative chambers, and the Nebraska state investment officer. Funding/appropriations: general operations are to be appropriated equally by compacting states when authorized by their legislatures; the commission may accept gifts, grants, and appropriations from federal, state, local governments, agencies, municipalities, and private parties; it may not issue debt and must submit budgets to the officer designated by each party state. Nebraska-specific provisions: Nebraska must enact a legislative bill before participating in or appropriating funds for any compact rail project (including planning). A Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact Cash Fund is created; funds may be invested by the state investment officer under Nebraska investment law. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB259_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB259_Intro_Copy.docx LB259 (Faithful Delegate to Federal Article V Convention Act) establishes procedures for Nebraska’s participation in a federal Article V convention. Key state entities/roles: the Nebraska Legislature (elects delegates and alternate delegates via Committee on Committees nominations), the Article V Convention Committee (delegates form committee; Legislature elects chair and vice-chair), the Executive Board of the Legislative Council and the Lieutenant Governor (serve as the advisory committee; chair of the executive board serves as advisory chair; Lt. Gov. may break ties), and the Secretary of State (files delegates’ oaths). The bill references state expense reimbursement statutes (sections 81-1174 to 81-1177) and the Nebraska Political Accountability and Disclosure Act (gift prohibition from registered lobbyists; Class III misdemeanor penalty). It also requires notification by the Speaker to the convention presiding officer of any disqualified delegate. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Creates procedures for Nebraska's Article V convention delegation. Key state entities: the Nebraska Legislature (which elects delegates/alternates, adopts instructions, and determines unauthorized votes); the Committee on Committees (nominates delegates); the Article V Convention Committee (delegates constitute this committee); the Executive Board of the Legislative Council and the Lieutenant Governor (serve as the advisory committee, chair is executive‑board chair, Lt. Governor breaks ties); the Speaker of the Legislature (must notify committee chair and convention presiding officer of disqualifications); and the Secretary of State (files delegates' oaths). Federal officer offices (Secretary of the U.S. Senate, Clerk of the U.S. House) are referenced for lobbyist reporting. Delegates receive no compensation but may be reimbursed under existing statutes (secs. 81‑1174 to 81‑1177). No new appropriations or budget allocations are made. Gift restrictions and a Class III misdemeanor penalty are included. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB265_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB265_Final_Copy.docx Department of Administrative Services, Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor, Department of Health and Human Services The bill centralizes workforce/unemployment funding under the Department of Labor (DOL): the State Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund, Nebraska Training and Support Cash Fund, and Sector Partnership Program Fund terminate July 1, 2025, with balances and future state UI tax receipts redirected into a new Workforce Development Program Cash Fund administered by DOL. The commissioner sets UI tax rates; the fund may finance workforce grants, administration, unemployment benefits, studies, and a Manufacturing Modernization and Workforce Development Pilot (pilot grants up to $250,000). The final average combined tax rate is reduced 5% for 2025–2029. Sec. 20 directs a $2,950,000 transfer from the Workforce Fund to the General Fund. The Department of Economic Development (DED) assumes the Job Training Cash Fund and it may receive Cash Reserve Fund transfers; DAS is directed to transfer $20,000,000 to the Economic Development Cash Fund. The Department of Administrative Services (DAS) budget administrator schedules multiple interfund transfers, including $440,000,000 GF→Cash Reserve Fund and transfers totaling $14,820,000 to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) Cash Fund; DHHS is identified as hospital licensing authority. - Department of Economic Development: creates a Manufacturing Modernization and Workforce Development Pilot (applications Oct 1, 2025–Nov 1, 2026). Eligible manufacturers must document project, cost, and private matching funds at least equal to the grant. Grants equal the private match, capped at $50,000 per applicant; total pilot awards capped at $250,000 from the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund. Grants must not fund projects begun before application; repayment required if eligibility lapses. Department may adopt rules.\n\n- Department of Labor: clarifies permitted uses of the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund (including the pilot, grants, admin, unemployment tax/benefit costs, and labor studies). Nebraska Workforce Development Board may submit up to 18 proposals yearly to the Commissioner, who may approve/reject/modify and may approve up to 3 without board approval (reporting required if approvals exceed 25% of unobligated balance).\n\n- Department of Administrative Services: budget administrator directs timing/amounts of transfers — $2,950,000 from the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund to the General Fund (FY2025‑26) and $5,000,000 from Cash Reserve to the General Fund (FY2026‑27).\n\n- Department of Health and Human Services: no substantive changes or funding actions referenced. 109-1-LB266_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB266_Final_Copy.docx LB266 prohibits local governments — defined as any city, village, county, or any agency or subdivision thereof — from enacting or enforcing ordinances that have the effect of imposing rent controls on private property. "Ordinance" is broadly defined to include any local law, resolution, rule, or regulation. Exceptions allow land‑use or inclusionary housing requirements adopted to increase affordable housing and voluntary, contractual programs in which property owners agree to restrict rents. The prohibition overrides home‑rule charters, and any ordinance violating the statute is declared null and void. Referred committee: Government, Military and Veterans Affairs. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Defines "local government" to include any city, village, county or any agency or subdivision thereof, and prohibits those local governments from enacting or enforcing ordinances that impose rent control on private property, except: (a) land‑use or inclusionary housing ordinances adopted to increase affordable housing; or (b) voluntary, contract‑based programs in which private owners agree to limit rents. The provision overrides home rule charters and renders violating ordinances null and void. No state agencies are named and no funding or appropriations are affected. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB267_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB267_Intro_Copy.docx Bill amends the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to allow tenants to remove a cotenant or occupant who commits domestic violence (with protective order or certified verification) and to require landlords to change locks when the perpetrator is non-cotenant. Relevant government actors and duties:\n- Courts: landlords may file suit for recovery of possession against the perpetrator; if judgment favors the landlord, the landlord may recover court costs and reasonable attorney’s fees from the perpetrator.\n- Law enforcement: landlords must refuse perpetrator access to reclaim property unless escorted by a law enforcement officer.\nNo state agency appropriations or budget allocations are included. Adds tenant protections allowing removal of a cotenant perpetrator of domestic violence (with a protective order or certified domestic-violence documentation) by notification to the landlord and triggering the five‑day removal process under section 76‑1431. Landlord obligations include serving the five‑day notice, pursuing possession suit against the perpetrator if they fail to vacate, installing new locks (per section 3), notifying the tenant how to regain access, and refusing perpetrator access unless escorted by a law enforcement officer. If judgment favors the landlord, the court may award court costs and reasonable attorney fees to the landlord. For non‑cotenant perpetrators, a tenant with a protective order/certification may require the landlord to change or rekey locks within 24 hours; if the landlord fails to act, the tenant may change locks and must provide the landlord access. No state agencies beyond courts and law enforcement are named; no funding or appropriations are provided. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB272_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB272_Intro_Copy.docx LB272 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-3506 to expand homestead property-tax exemptions. Beginning January 1, 2026, the bill adds veterans rated at least 10% but less than 100% service‑connected disabled (and their qualifying surviving spouses) to eligible classes; the exemption for these veterans is a percentage of the exempt amount equal to the veteran’s VA disability rating. The United States Department of Veterans Affairs is specified as the source for required certification of veteran status. The bill also adjusts application/certification timing: applicants under subdivision (2)(a) must provide certification every fifth year, while applicants under (2)(b)–(g) must apply annually but need VA certification only every fifth year. No state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed. Adds a pro rata homestead tax exemption tied to a veteran’s disability rating: the exempt amount for homesteads described in subdivision (2)(g) will equal the veteran’s VA disability percentage. Effective January 1, 2026, expands eligibility to veterans discharged honorable or general (under honorable conditions) who receive compensation from the United States Department of Veterans Affairs for a service‑connected disability rated at least 10% but less than 100%, and who are not already eligible for total exemption under sections 77‑3526 to 77‑3528; it also covers an unremarried surviving spouse and a surviving spouse who remarries after age 57. No agencies beyond the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs are added, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB273_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB273_Intro_Copy.docx LB273 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §30-3417 governing attorneys-in-fact under powers of attorney for health care. It clarifies that county courts retain authority to determine a principal’s incapacity (per §30-3412) — a court finding is required before a principal’s objection yields to the attorney-in-fact — and requires health care providers to have a signed original or copy of the power of attorney before accepting decisions. The bill also limits an attorney-in-fact’s authority in specified end-of-life and pregnancy-related situations and affirms access to medical records. The original section is repealed. No state agencies, departments, or budget appropriations/funding changes are created or modified. Adds language conditioning an action that would likely cause death of the principal’s unborn child: such an action is barred unless the principal’s treating physician determines the principal’s life is at risk. No government agencies or departments are referenced and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB274_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB274_Intro_Copy.docx LB274 amends the Child Care Licensing Act’s oversight and screening procedures. The department must obtain written proof of liability insurance of at least $200,000 per occurrence before issuing a license and verify current coverage at unannounced inspections; failure to produce proof within three business days results in license suspension until coverage is verified. The department may investigate applicants and inspect facilities, may delegate environmental health inspections to local personnel, and may request State Fire Marshal fire-safety inspections (with notification when authority is delegated). Nebraska State Patrol will collect fingerprints and transmit them to the FBI for national criminal history checks; the department will provide eligibility documentation and will seek federal funds to offset fingerprinting costs, though no new state appropriations or budget allocations are specified. Adds requirements that inspectors must request and verify current proof of required liability insurance at each unannounced inspection and each investigation. If a licensee cannot produce proof or lets coverage lapse, "the department" must notify the licensee and allow three business days to provide proof; failure to do so results in license suspension. Licenses are reinstated when the department receives and verifies current insurance per section 71-1911.03. The provision references section 71-1911.03; no specific agency beyond "the department" and inspectors is named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB275_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB275_Final_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill amends §43-907 to impose multiple duties on the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) regarding children under its charge. Key provisions require DHHS to: screen each child for Social Security eligibility within 60 days and apply/appeal on the child's behalf; serve as representative payee when appropriate and manage/hold benefit payments separate from department funds consistent with federal law; report receipt, conservation, and expenditures to the juvenile court at each review and provide accounting on request; consult beneficiaries age 14+ semiannually; conserve specified minimum percentages of benefits by age (14+: 20%; 16+: 30%; 17+: 40%; 18+: 50%); create a public form and adopt rules by Oct 1, 2026; and seek maximal federal Title IV‑E funding before using General Funds for implementation costs. Creates duties for the Department of Health and Human Services to screen children in its care for Social Security benefit eligibility within 60 days, file and, if needed, appeal applications on their behalf, and provide age‑appropriate written notice and accounting to children and representatives. If the department acts as representative payee it must manage payments per federal law, keep funds separate (generally in trust), use accounts that avoid federal resource limits (e.g., ABLE, special‑needs trusts), and conserve minimum percentages of benefits by age (14+: 20%; 16+: 30%; 17+: 40%; 18+: 50%). For beneficiaries 14+, the department must consult at least semiannually, assist with benefit continuity six months before exit, and notify exiting children about retained funds and payee status. A public request form is due by Oct 1, 2026. Fiscal: department must maximize federal Title IV‑E funding before using General Funds; no specific appropriation amounts included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB276_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB276_Intro_Copy.docx LB276 creates the Municipal Police Oversight Act and revises duties for multiple state and local law-enforcement entities.\n\nKey agency responsibilities:\n- Cities (metropolitan/primary class) must establish seven-member citizen police oversight boards by Jan 1, 2028; boards may investigate complaints and shootings, inspect police records, issue subpoenas, consult standards from the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice and the Nebraska Police Standards Advisory Council, and publish findings. Police departments must respond to recommendations; oversight records are public and meetings follow the Open Meetings Act.\n- City attorneys, county attorneys, and the Attorney General must maintain and post monthly Brady/Giglio lists; the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice must adopt implementing rules by Sept 1, 2025.\n- Judges/magistrates are prohibited from issuing no‑knock warrants.\n- Chiefs/sheriffs/agency heads must file personnel-status forms with the training‑center director within seven days, retain separation records, permanently retain misconduct records subject to commission review, and report terminations/resignations in lieu to the commission within 30 days. The commission must publicly post officer decertification/conviction/misconduct lists with details and a challenge procedure.\n\nNo funding or appropriation changes are included. The act takes effect immediately. Creates mandatory municipal citizen police oversight boards (seven public members, appointed by city council) by Jan 1, 2028, with powers to investigate shootings, misconduct, discrimination, and employee complaints; inspect all police records (including personnel files) notwithstanding other law; issue subpoenas (court-enforceable); refer suspected criminal conduct to the county attorney; and report findings to the city police department, mayor, city council and federal/state registries. Oversight boards and investigators must consult standards from the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice and the Nebraska Police Standards Advisory Council. All reports are public records; meetings fall under the Open Meetings Act. Cities may not contract or bargain away board authority. Beginning Sept 1, 2025, city attorneys, county attorneys, and the Attorney General must maintain and publicly post monthly Brady/Giglio officer lists; the Commission must adopt implementing rules by that date. No funding or appropriations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB277_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB277_Intro_Copy.docx LB277 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §29-1401 to require district courts to convene a grand jury when the county coroner or coroner’s physician certifies a death occurred while a person was being apprehended by, or in the custody of, law enforcement or detention personnel. The court must appoint a special prosecutor with at least five years’ felony/criminal litigation experience who will select a three-officer homicide-investigation team from outside the jurisdiction to examine evidence and report to the special prosecutor. Local law enforcement must secure the scene and investigate until evidence is transferred. A grand jury must be impaneled within 30 days unless extended for compelling reasons. If a licensed physician certifies natural causes and the county attorney presents that finding to a grand jury, a special prosecutor need not be appointed. Officers involved may not return to duty until the grand jury completes its investigation. No appropriations or funding changes are included. Adds a requirement that the court appoint a special prosecutor with at least five years’ experience in criminal litigation, including felony work. It also includes language about exceptions for jurisdictions outside the immediate jurisdiction (text is partially unclear) regarding when a special prosecutor need not be appointed. Requires that any law enforcement officers or detention personnel involved in a death may not return to duty until the grand jury completes its investigation. No state agencies beyond courts, grand juries, law enforcement, and detention personnel are newly created or referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes in the added text.
